abstract: We prove the P\'olya--Szeg\H{o} buckling conjecture in dimensions $2\le n\le47$: among open sets of prescribed finite volume, a ball minimizes the first clamped buckling eigenvalue. More precisely, we establish the sharp comparison $\Lambda_1\left(\Omega\right)\ge \left(j_{n/2,1}/j_{n/2-1,1}\right)^2 \lambda_1^{\mathrm D}\left(\Omega\right)$, where $\lambda_1^{\mathrm D}$ is the first Dirichlet eigenvalue and $j_{\nu,1}$ is the first positive zero of the Bessel function $J_\nu$ of the first kind. The proof extends a radial calibration to all Hessian directions; positive coefficient expansions and logarithmically convex Laplace integrals control the resulting matrix. A Lipschitz construction handles sign changes and arbitrary boundaries. Equality in the volume bound holds precisely for balls modulo sets of zero $H^2$ capacity. We prove that this calibration fails in every dimension $n\ge48$.
hook: A ball has the lowest buckling eigenvalue among shapes of equal volume, proved for dimensions 2 to 47.
summary: The authors prove the Polya-Szego buckling conjecture: among regions of fixed volume, a ball has the smallest first buckling eigenvalue, which measures how easily a clamped plate buckles. They compare it with the first Dirichlet eigenvalue using a calibration argument that works in every Hessian direction. The method provably fails in dimension 48 and above, so higher dimensions stay open.
title: The P\'{o}lya--Szeg\H{o} buckling conjecture in dimensions two through forty-seven
